gist: The Word was God, or the Word was a god. The difference is one missing article.

lemma: εἰμί eimi · G1510 / γίνομαι ginomai · G1096
gist: Was, and came to be. Two verbs one verse apart, and the whole prologue turns on the difference.
The Word was with God. The preposition is not the one you would expect for with.
Why call a person a Word? The Greek noun covers far more than a unit of speech, and two different backgrounds are competing for it.
The darkness did not comprehend it, or did not overcome it. The verb means both and John probably wanted both.
Coming into the world. Nothing in the Greek tells you whether that describes the light or the man.
Power to become the sons of God. The word is closer to right or authority than to power.
Not of blood. The Greek says bloods, plural, and the plural is a Hebrew way of speaking.
Dwelt among us. The verb is built on the word for tent, and the whole Old Testament is inside it.

lemma: χάρις charis · G5485 / ἀλήθεια aletheia · G225
gist: Full of grace and truth. That is a Hebrew pair, and it comes from Exodus 34.
Grace for grace. The preposition normally means instead of, which makes the phrase hard rather than warm.
The only begotten Son, or the only begotten God. The manuscripts do not agree and the difference is enormous.

lemma: Μεσσίας Messias · G3323 / Κηφᾶς Kephas · G2786
gist: John stops the narrative twice to translate a word for you, which tells you who he thought was reading.
Verily I say unto you. The you is plural, and Jesus has been talking to one man.

lemma: τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ti emoi kai soi
gist: What have I to do with thee. A Hebrew idiom carried word for word into Greek.
Mine hour is not yet come. A word John uses as a countdown to one event.
The beginning of miracles. John's word is sign, and he never uses the usual word for miracle.
A scourge of small cords. The noun occurs once in the New Testament and is a Latin word in Greek dress.
The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up. The verb is consume, and the tense was changed in the quotation.

lemma: ναός naos · G3485 / ἱερόν hieron · G2411
gist: Destroy this temple. Greek has two words for temple and this is the inner one.
Many believed. And Jesus did not believe them. The same verb, twice, deliberately.
Born again, or born from above. The Greek word means both and Nicodemus hears only one.
Born of water and of the Spirit. One preposition governs both nouns, or two.
The wind blows where it wills. Wind and Spirit are the same Greek word, and the sentence needs both at once.
Who is in heaven. Three words that are in some manuscripts and not others.
Believeth in him. The phrase can attach to believe or to eternal life.
For God so loved the world. So means in this way, not so very much.
Everlasting life. The Greek adjective is built on the word for age, not the word for endless.

lemma: κρίνω krino · G2919 / κρίσις krisis · G2920
gist: Condemned already. The Greek word is judged, and the noun in the next verse is the judgment.
The friend of the bridegroom. A defined role in Jewish weddings, not a figure of speech.
Where does the speech end? Greek manuscripts have no quotation marks.
He that believeth not. The Greek verb in the second half is disobey, not disbelieve.
The sixth hour. Which clock John is using is an old and unresolved question.
Have no dealings with. A rare verb, and it may mean do not share vessels.
Living water. In ordinary speech it means running water from a spring.
True worshippers. The adjective means real as against counterfeit, not sincere.
God is spirit. Same construction as the last clause of John 1:1, and here nobody reads it as a god.
I that speak unto thee am he. The Greek is the same two words as John 8:58.
White already to harvest. The colour word points at ripeness, and the verb is a command to look.
Bethesda. The manuscripts do not agree on the name of the pool.
The angel troubling the water. A whole verse that is not in the oldest manuscripts.

lemma: ἴσον τῷ θεῷ ison to theo
gist: Making himself equal with God. The charge is the narrator's report of what they heard.
Because he is the Son of man. No article, and John never does this anywhere else.
Search the scriptures. The Greek form is both a command and a statement.
Him hath God the Father sealed. A commercial and legal word for marking ownership.
I am the bread of life. The first of the predicate I am sayings.
Except the Father draw him. The verb is used of hauling a net and drawing a sword.
Whoso eateth my flesh. The verb changes at verse 54 to a word for chewing.
The flesh profiteth nothing. Said immediately after a discourse about eating flesh.
One of you is a devil. The Greek noun is slanderer, and it has no article here.
I go not up yet unto this feast. Some manuscripts lack the word yet.
Out of his belly shall flow rivers. Whose belly depends on where the sentence is punctuated.
The Holy Ghost was not yet given. The word given is not in the Greek.
The woman taken in adultery. The best manuscripts do not have this passage.

lemma: ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου
gist: I am the light of the world. Said during a festival lit by enormous lamps.
If ye believe not that I am. Twice in five verses, with nothing after it.

lemma: ἐλευθερόω eleutheroo · G1659 / δοῦλος doulos · G1401
gist: The truth shall make you free. And the next sentence is about slavery, not about employment.
A liar, and the father of it. The pronoun could be of it or of him.
Rejoiced to see my day. The verb is closer to exulted, and the seeing is aorist.

lemma: ἐγώ εἰμι ego eimi · G1473 + G1510
gist: Before Abraham was, I am. The verb is wrong on purpose.
Siloam, which is by interpretation, Sent. John stops to translate again.
Put out of the synagogue. A compound word that appears nowhere before John.
Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him. Some manuscripts do not have it.
The good shepherd. The adjective is not the ordinary word for good.

lemma: αὐλή aule · G833 / ποίμνη poimne · G4167
gist: One fold, and one shepherd. The Greek uses two different nouns and the King James uses one.
My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all. The manuscripts disagree about what is greater.

lemma: φιλέω phileo · G5368 / ἀγαπάω agapao · G25
gist: Both love-words, one chapter, the same relationship. Whatever they are doing, they are not ranking it.
He groaned in the spirit. The verb is an anger word, not a grief word.
Jesus wept. A different verb from the weeping of everyone else in the scene.
The Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.
Ointment of spikenard, very costly. The adjective is a word nobody has settled.
I will draw all men unto me. The same verb as the drawing in chapter six.
When he saw his glory. Some manuscripts read when, others read because.
He loved them unto the end. To the finish, or to the utmost.
He that is washed needeth not save to wash his feet. Some copies lack the feet.
A new commandment. The word for new means fresh in kind, not recent in time.
Ye believe in God, believe also in me. Both verbs could be statements or commands.
In my Father's house are many mansions. The noun means a place to stay.
Comforter, Helper, Advocate, Counselor, Paraclete. Six versions, six words, one Greek noun nobody can carry.
Every branch that beareth not fruit he taketh away. The verb also means lifts up.
Without me ye can do nothing. The preposition is closer to apart from.
Reprove the world of sin. One verb, three objects, and no agreed rendering.
He will shew you things to come. The verb is announce, and the phrase need not mean prediction.
This is life eternal, that they might know thee. Knowing here is relational, not informational.
The glory which I had with thee before the world was. Glory again, and para with the dative.
I am he. And they went backward and fell to the ground.
Lest they should be defiled. A purity concern stated without explanation.
The Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha. Another gloss, in the other direction.
Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull. And John says it the other way round.
It is finished. One word, in a tense that means done and still in force.
Touch me not. The Greek is stop doing what you are already doing.

lemma: ὁ κύριός μου καὶ ὁ θεός μου
gist: My Lord and my God. Both nouns have the article, which is the point.

lemma: ἀγαπάω agapao · G25 / φιλέω phileo · G5368
gist: Two different Greek words for love, and the sermon you have heard about them is probably overselling it.

lemma: βόσκω bosko · G1006 / ποιμαίνω poimaino · G4165
gist: Feed my lambs, tend my sheep. Four words vary, not two.
In the beginning, or when God began. The first word is shaped like half a phrase.
Created. A verb with only one possible subject in the whole Hebrew Bible.

lemma: שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ shamayim wa-arets · H8064 + H776
gist: The heaven and the earth. Not two items. One idea named by its opposite ends.
Moved, hovered, or swept. One rare verb and a bird.

lemma: יוֹם אֶחָד yom echad · H3117 + H259
gist: The first day. Literally, one day, a cardinal number, while every later day uses an ordinal.

lemma: רָקִיעַ raqia (רָקַע raqa, to beat out) · H7549
gist: Let there be a firmament. A word built on the sense of beating something out flat, likely naming a solid dome, not empty space.
Let them be for signs, and for seasons. Moedim, the same word later naming Israel's appointed feasts.

lemma: הַמָּאוֹר הַגָּדֹל / הַקָּטֹן hama'or hagadol / hakaton (cf. שֶׁמֶשׁ shemesh, יָרֵחַ yareach) · H3974 / H8121 / H3394
gist: The greater light and the lesser light. Not shemesh, sun, and yareach, moon, the same words as the sun-god and moon-god.
God created great whales. The Hebrew word, tannin, elsewhere names the mythological sea-monster Leviathan.
Let us make. A plural announcement followed immediately by a singular act.

lemma: צֶלֶם tselem · H6754 / דְּמוּת demut · H1823
gist: In our image, after our likeness. Two nouns, and probably one idea.

lemma: כָּבַשׁ kabash / רָדָה radah · H3533 / H7287
gist: Subdue it, and have dominion. Forceful, even military and royal vocabulary, standing beside Genesis 2's gentler verbs for the same job.
God rested. The verb means stopped, not recovered.
These are the generations. A recurring formula, not a genealogy header.
In the day that the LORD God made. An idiom meaning when, not a calendar entry.
A mist went up. A word used only here and once in Job, and nobody is certain what it names.
Breathed into his nostrils the breath of life. A different word from the one in chapter one.

lemma: נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה nephesh chayyah · H5315 + H2416
gist: Man became a living soul. The same phrase is used of the animals.

lemma: עָבַד abad · H5647 / שָׁמַר shamar · H8104
gist: To work it and keep it. The same two verbs describe the Levites guarding the tabernacle.

lemma: מוֹת תָּמוּת mot tamut (מוּת muth) · H4191
gist: Thou shalt surely die. Literally dying, you shall die: the verb said twice.

lemma: עֵזֶר ezer · H5828 / נֶגֶד neged · H5048
gist: Help meet. Two English words that were never one word, and a Hebrew phrase that says something else again.
One of his ribs. The same word names the side chambers of the tabernacle everywhere else.

lemma: אִישׁ ish · H376 / אִשָּׁה ishah · H802
gist: She shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. A pun that sounds like a derivation.

lemma: בָּשָׂר אֶחָד basar echad · H1320 + H259
gist: One flesh. A kinship word, not only a body word.

lemma: עָרוֹם arom · H6174 / עָרוּם arum · H6175
gist: Naked, and not ashamed. Then: the serpent was more crafty. Two words that are near-twins in Hebrew.
The cool of the day. The Hebrew word is the same one translated Spirit.

lemma: הוּא hu (with זֶרַע zera) · H1931 / H2233
gist: He shall bruise thy head. The Hebrew pronoun is unambiguously masculine, singular, he.
It shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. Same verb, four occurrences total, and bruise may be too gentle for either half.
Sorrow in childbearing, toil in the field. One Hebrew word, two English words.
Thy desire shall be to thy husband. Three occurrences in the whole Bible, and they do not agree.

lemma: חַוָּה Chavah · H2332 (חָיָה chayah, to live · H2421)
gist: He called her Eve, because she was the mother of all living. The name means life.
A flaming sword which turned every way. The verb form says the sword turns itself.

lemma: אֶת et (with קָנִיתִי qaniti, I have gotten) · H853 / H7069
gist: I have gotten a man from the LORD. Or: a man, the LORD. The little word between them decides which.

lemma: רֹבֵץ rovets (רָבַץ ravats) · H7257 / תְּשׁוּקָה teshuqah, מָשַׁל mashal · H8669, H4910
gist: Sin lieth at the door. Its desire is to thee, and thou shalt rule over it. The same crouching-word, and the same two words as 3:16.

lemma: וַיֹּאמֶר vayomer (אמר amar, to say) · H559
gist: Cain talked with Abel his brother. The Hebrew text never says what he said; other ancient witnesses supply Let us go into the field.
Thy brother's blood crieth. The Hebrew word is plural, bloods, and English cannot say that.

lemma: נָע וָנָד na vanad (נוּעַ nua, נוּד nud) · H5128, H5110
gist: A fugitive and a vagabond. Cain then dwells in the land of Nod, wandering, the same word as his curse.

lemma: הָרַגְתִּי haragti (הָרַג harag, to kill) · H2026
gist: I have slain a man. Or: I would slay a man. The same Hebrew perfect tense supports both.

lemma: הוּחַל huchal (חָלַל chalal I, begin / III, profane) · H2490
gist: Then began men to call upon the name of the LORD. Or: then it became common, in a profaning sense, to call on that name.

lemma: וַיָּמֹת vayamot (מוּת muth, to die) · H4191
gist: And he died. The same two words end almost every entry in the genealogy, on purpose.
Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him. The refrain breaks, and the verb for walked is unusual.

lemma: נֹחַ Noach (נוּחַ nuach, rest) / נִחַם nacham, comfort · H5146, H5162
gist: He called his name Noah, saying, this shall comfort us. Comfort is nacham; the name Noah is built on the different word nuach, rest.

lemma: בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים bene ha'elohim · H1121 + H430
gist: The sons of God saw the daughters of men. The oldest reading takes sons of God as divine beings, not a human family line.

lemma: יָדוֹן yadon (roots proposed: דין din, judge, or דּוּן dun, remain) · H1777
gist: My spirit shall not always strive with man. A verb used only this once, and nobody is fully certain what it says God's spirit will stop doing.

lemma: נְפִלִים Nephilim (נָפַל naphal, to fall) · H5303
gist: There were giants in the earth. The Hebrew word, Nephilim, does not itself mean giant.
It repented the LORD. A verb that means comfort, grieve, relent and change course, all at once.

lemma: כֹּפֶר kopher / כָּפַר kaphar · H3724 / H3722
gist: Pitch it within and without with pitch. The noun for pitch and the verb for cover share the root behind atonement.
Gopher wood. A word used exactly once, and no one knows for certain what tree it names.
A window shalt thou make to the ark. The word may mean light or roof rather than an opening you look through.
By sevens, seven and seven. The Hebrew just repeats the numeral; English has to add a preposition to get the same sense.
The flood of waters. The word mabbul names only this flood, never an ordinary one.
The fountains of the great deep, and the windows of heaven. The word for deep is a cousin of the name of a Babylonian sea-goddess.
God remembered Noah. Not recalling a forgotten fact, but acting on a standing promise.

lemma: הָרֵי אֲרָרָט harei Ararat (הַר har, mountain, plural construct) · H2022 + H780
gist: The mountains of Ararat. A region, plural mountains, not a single named peak.

lemma: נִיחֹחַ nichoach (נוּחַ nuach, to rest) · H5207
gist: The LORD smelled a sweet savour. The word for sweet, soothing, shares Noah's own root.

lemma: יֵצֶר yetser (יָצַר yatsar, to form) · H3336
gist: The imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth. The same diagnosis as before the flood, now given as the reason God will not flood the earth again.
Flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat. Life and blood are named with the same word, nephesh.

lemma: שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם shofekh dam ha'adam (chiastic word order) · H8210 + H1818 + H120
gist: Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed. The Hebrew word order is a mirror around the center.

lemma: יַפְתְּ yapht (פָּתָה pathah, to make wide) / יֶפֶת Yephet · H6601 / H3315
gist: God shall enlarge Japheth. The verb for enlarge sounds like the name Japheth itself.
A mighty hunter before the LORD. Renowned in God's sight, or in open defiance of Him.

lemma: פֶּלֶג Peleg (פָּלַג palag, to divide) · H6389
gist: In his days was the earth divided. His name, Peleg, means division.
The whole earth was of one language. Literally, one lip, and one set of words.

lemma: וְרֹאשׁוֹ בַשָּׁמַיִם verosho vashamayim, its head in the heavens · H8064
gist: A tower whose top may reach unto heaven. Standard ancient building-inscription language, not a literal engineering claim.

lemma: בָּלַל balal (with בָּבֶל Bavel, cf. Akkadian bab-ilu) · H1101 / H894
gist: Therefore is the name of it called Babel, because the LORD did there confound. A pun that mocks the city's own name for itself.

lemma: לֶךְ־לְךָ lech lecha (הָלַךְ halach, to go) · H1980
gist: Get thee out. Literally go, for yourself, or go, to yourself: a pronoun added where none was grammatically needed.
In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed. Passive, or reflexive: blessed through you, or blessing themselves by your name.
The Canaanite was then in the land. The word then implies the writer already knows a time when the Canaanite was not.

lemma: אֵל עֶלְיוֹן El Elyon · H410 + H5945
gist: Melchizedek, priest of the most high God. A title shared with Canaanite religion, which Abraham treats as naming his own God.

lemma: מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק Malki-tsedek / שָׁלֵם Shalem · H4442 / H8004
gist: Melchizedek, king of Salem. His name means king of righteousness; Salem means peace.

lemma: בֶּן־מֶשֶׁק בֵּיתִי ben-meshek beythi · H1121 + H4943
gist: The steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus. A rare word, ben-meshek, that nobody fully agrees on.
He believed in the LORD. The verb is the root behind amen.
He counted it to him for righteousness. The verb belongs in a ledger.

lemma: כָּרַת בְּרִית karat berit · H3772 + H1285
gist: The LORD made a covenant with Abram. Literally, cut a covenant, and the chapter just showed you the cutting.

lemma: מַלְאַךְ יְהוָה malach YHWH · H4397 + H3068
gist: The angel of the LORD found Hagar. She then says the LORD spoke to her, and names him accordingly.

lemma: פֶּרֶא אָדָם pere adam · H6501 + H120
gist: He will be a wild man. The Hebrew literally reads a wild-donkey of a man, animal first.

lemma: אֵל שַׁדַּי El Shaddai · H410 + H7706
gist: I am the Almighty God. El Shaddai, a title whose root meaning is genuinely uncertain.

lemma: ה heh (in אַבְרָהָם Abraham and שָׂרָה Sarah) · cf. H3068 YHWH
gist: Abram becomes Abraham; Sarai becomes Sarah. Both gain the same Hebrew letter, heh, also found in God's own name.

lemma: צָחַק tsachak (יִצְחָק Yitzchak, Isaac) · H6711 / H3327
gist: Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed. The verb tsachak becomes his son's name, Yitzchak, Isaac, he laughs.

lemma: וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו יְהוָה vayera elav YHWH · H7200 + H3068
gist: The LORD appeared unto him. He lifted up his eyes, and lo, three men stood by him.
I know him, that he will command his children. Know here names a relationship, not a fact.

lemma: מֵאֵת יְהוָה מִן־הַשָּׁמָיִם me'et YHWH min hashamayim · H3068
gist: The LORD rained brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven. The LORD is named twice in one sentence.
His wife looked back from behind him. The verb is a deliberate, longing gaze, not a startled glance.

lemma: מוֹאָב Moab (cf. מֵאָב me'av, from a father) · H4124
gist: She called his name Moab. The name echoes me'av, from a father, memorializing how he was conceived.
He is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee. The word's first use in the Bible names an intercessor, not a predictor.
Sarah saw the son of Hagar mocking. The verb, metzachek, is built from the same root as Isaac's name.

lemma: בְּאֵר שֶׁבַע Be'er Sheva (שֶׁבַע sheva, seven / שָׁבַע shava, swear) · H884
gist: Beersheba, well of the oath, or well of seven. One root, sheva, carries both meanings.
God did tempt Abraham. The Hebrew verb means tested or proved, not enticed toward evil.
Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac. Abraham already has another living son, Ishmael.
The LORD will provide. The Hebrew verb is see, and the chapter has been using it all along.

lemma: נְשִׂיא אֱלֹהִים nesi elohim · H5387 + H430
gist: A mighty prince among us. Literally, a prince of God, using elohim as a superlative.
The longest chapter in Genesis is long because the same story gets told twice, almost word for word.
Abraham gave up the ghost. One Hebrew verb, meaning expired or breathed his last; ghost has since become a word for a spirit-apparition.
The children struggled together within her. A rare, violent verb: crushing, not merely kicking.

lemma: וְרַב יַעֲבֹד צָעִיר verav ya'avod tsa'ir · H7227 + H5647 + H6810
gist: The elder shall serve the younger. Or: the elder, shall the younger serve. The Hebrew word order does not decide it.

lemma: אַדְמוֹנִי admoni / אָדֹם adom / אֱדוֹם Edom · H132 / H122
gist: Esau, red at birth. Edom, from the red stew he later sells his birthright for. One Hebrew color word, twice.

lemma: יַעֲקֹב Ya'akov (עָקֵב akev, heel / עָקַב akav, deceive) · H3290 / H6117
gist: His hand took hold on Esau's heel, and his name was called Jacob. The same root also means deceiver, supplanter.
Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife. The same root as laughed and mocked, now meaning caressed or fondled.

lemma: שִׂטְנָה Sitnah (cf. שָׂטָן satan) · H7856 / H7854
gist: He called the name of the well Sitnah. The same root behind the word Satan.
A ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven. A word used only here, likely naming a staircase like a ziggurat's.

lemma: רַכּוֹת rakkot (רַךְ rakh, soft, tender) · H7390
gist: Leah was tender eyed. The word could mean weak, or it could mean soft and lovely.

lemma: (eleven birth-name puns; see individual roots in the Sources)
gist: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph. Each name is a stated pun on the mother's words at his birth.

lemma: יוֹסֵף Yoseph (יָסַף yasaph, add / אָסַף asaph, take away) · H3130 / H3254 / H622
gist: She called his name Joseph, saying, the LORD shall add to me another son. A second, earlier pun on the same name used a different root, for taking away.
Rachel had stolen the images. Household gods whose possession, per comparable ancient legal custom, could carry inheritance rights.

lemma: יְגַר שָׂהֲדוּתָא Yegar Sahaduta (Aramaic) / גַּלְעֵד Gal-ed (Hebrew) · H3026 / H1567
gist: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha; Jacob called it Galeed. Two languages, same meaning, spoken by two members of the same extended family.
The LORD watch between me and thee. Not a blessing of closeness; a warning born of mutual distrust.

lemma: יִשְׂרָאֵל Yisrael (שָׂרָה sarah, strive + אֵל el, God) · H3478
gist: Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God. The name itself could mean he strives with God, or God strives.

lemma: פְּנִיאֵל Peniel (פָּנִים panim, face + אֵל el, God) · H6439
gist: Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face.

lemma: רָב rav / כֹּל kol · H7227 / H3605
gist: Esau said, I have enough. Jacob said, I have all things. Two different Hebrew words, rav and kol, for two different postures toward wealth.
And defiled her. The verb anah is used elsewhere explicitly for rape, and elsewhere more broadly for affliction.
He had wrought folly in Israel. A fixed idiom for a grave sexual offense, not an improvised phrase.

lemma: בֶּן־אוֹנִי Ben-oni (אוֹן on, sorrow) / בִּנְיָמִין Binyamin (יָמִין yamin, right hand) · H1126 / H1144
gist: She called his name Ben-oni: but his father called him Benjamin. Son of my sorrow, overridden by son of the right hand.
He found the yemim in the wilderness. A word used once, translated as mules by some, hot springs by others.

lemma: לִפְנֵי מְלָךְ־מֶלֶךְ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל lifney meloch melech livney Yisrael · H4427
gist: These are the kings that reigned in Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel. The comparison assumes Israel already has kings.

lemma: כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים ketonet passim · H3801 + H6446
gist: A coat of many colours. Modern scholarship increasingly favors a long-sleeved robe, not a rainbow garment.

lemma: יִשְׁמְעֵאלִים Yishme'elim / מִדְיָנִים Midyanim · H3459 / H4084
gist: Ishmeelites and Midianites both appear as Joseph's captors within the same short passage.
I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Sheol, whose precise nature the Old Testament never fully defines.

lemma: פֶּתַח עֵינַיִם Petach Eynayim · H6607 + H5879
gist: She sat in an open place. The Hebrew could be a place name, Enaim, or literally the opening of the eyes.

lemma: וַיְהִי יְהוָה אִתּוֹ vayehi YHWH ito · H3068
gist: The LORD was with Joseph. A recurring formula that replaces direct divine speech for the rest of the book.

lemma: יִשָּׂא פַרְעֹה אֶת־רֹאשֶׁךָ yissa Pharaoh et rosh'cha · H5375 + H7218
gist: Pharaoh shall lift up thine head. For the butler, restored to office. For the baker, the same phrase, with one word added, means beheaded.
Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnath-paaneah. An Egyptian name whose meaning remains genuinely disputed.

lemma: מְנַשֶּׁה Menashsheh (נָשָׁה nashah, forget) / אֶפְרַיִם Ephraim (פָּרָה parah, fruitful) · H4519 / H5382 / H669 / H6509
gist: Manasseh, for God hath made me forget; Ephraim, for God hath caused me to be fruitful. Two more names built from the naming sentence itself.
He spake unto them by an interpreter. The same root, melitz, later names a mediator or advocate in Job.

lemma: נֶפֶשׁ קְשׁוּרָה nephesh keshurah · H5315 + H7194
gist: His life is bound up in the lad's life. Nephesh, the same word as living soul, used twice, bound together.

lemma: אָב לְפַרְעֹה av le-Pharaoh · H1 + H6547
gist: He hath made me a father to Pharaoh. An Egyptian administrative title, not a family claim.
Jacob's heart fainted. A rare verb some read as his heart simply stopped, not merely swooned.

lemma: עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה ad hayom hazeh (idiom) · H3117
gist: Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt unto this day. A phrase marking the narrator's own, later vantage point.
Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh. An oath sworn on the organ of generation, not literally the thigh.

lemma: הַמַּלְאָךְ הַגֹּאֵל hamal'ach hago'el (גָּאַל ga'al, redeem) · H1350
gist: The Angel which redeemed me from all evil. The first use of go'el, redeemer, in the Bible, applied to an angel.

lemma: שְׁכֶם אֶחָד shechem echad (cf. שְׁכֶם Shechem) · H7926 / H7927
gist: I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren. Literally, one shechem, the same word as the city Shechem.

lemma: שור shor (ox) / שוּר shur (wall) · H7794 / H7791
gist: They digged down a wall. Or: they hamstrung oxen. The consonants are the same; only the vowels, added centuries later, decide.
Until Shiloh come. A word read as a place, a title, or a messianic figure, and translators still disagree.
Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good. The same verb, chashav, reckon, used of Abraham's faith at 15:6.
He was put in a coffin in Egypt. The Hebrew word, aron, is the same word later used for the Ark of the Covenant.
Blessed is the man. The Hebrew is a plural exclamation, not a description.
In his law doth he meditate day and night. The verb, hagah, means mutter or growl, not silent reflection.

lemma: הַיּוֹם יְלִדְתִּיךָ hayom yelidtikha (הַיּוֹם hayom, this day) · H3117 + H3205
gist: This day have I begotten thee. A coronation formula marking a specific day, not a timeless statement.

lemma: נַשְּׁקוּ־בַר nashequ bar (בַּר bar, Aramaic 'son' / Hebrew 'pure') · H1247 / H1249
gist: Kiss the Son. Or: kiss purely, do homage in purity. The word bar is Aramaic for son, but also Hebrew for grain, clean, or pure.
Selah. A notation appearing seventy-one times in the Psalms whose exact meaning nobody today can confirm.
A Shiggaion of David. A label used only twice in the whole Bible, with no confirmed meaning.
A little lower than the angels. The Hebrew says elohim.
The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. Nabal names moral corruption, not stupidity.
Neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption. Shachat most literally means pit, the grave, with decay only as an extension.

lemma: אִישׁוֹן בַּת־עַיִן ishon bat-ayin · H380 + H1323 + H5869
gist: Keep me as the apple of the eye. Literally, the little man, or the daughter of the eye: the pupil.
The heavens declare the glory of God. The Hebrew noun means weight before it means brightness.

lemma: קַו qav (line) / קוֹל qol (voice) · H6957 / H6963
gist: Their line is gone out through all the earth. Paul quotes it in Romans 10:18 as their voice, or sound.

lemma: אֵלִי אֵלִי לָמָה עֲזַבְתָּנִי Eli Eli lamah azavtani (Hebrew) / שְׁבַקְתַּנִי shevaqtani (Aramaic, behind sabachthani)
gist: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? The Gospels' version mixes Hebrew Eli with an Aramaic verb, not the Psalm's own Hebrew azavtani.

lemma: כָּאֲרוּ / כָּאֲרִי ka'aru / ka'ari · H3738 / H738
gist: They pierced my hands and my feet, or like a lion. One letter, and it is the wrong length in some copies.

lemma: צַלְמָוֶת tsalmavet (צֵל tsel, shadow + מָוֶת mavet, death, or one intensive noun) · H6757
gist: The valley of the shadow of death. Possibly not shadow plus death at all, but one word meaning deepest darkness.

lemma: שׁוּב shuv · H7725 / יָשַׁב yashav · H3427
gist: I will dwell in the house of the LORD. The consonants also allow I will return.
Goodness and mercy shall follow me. Mercy is chesed, and mercy is the weakest word for it.
I had fainted, unless I had believed. The Hebrew leaves the unless-clause without its other half.

lemma: בְּנֵי אֵלִים bene elim · H1121 + H410
gist: Ascribe unto the LORD, O ye mighty. Literally, sons of the elim, gods, the divine council again.

lemma: כְּסוּי kesui (כָּסָה kasah, cover; cf. כָּפַר kaphar, atone) · H3680 / H3722
gist: Blessed is he whose sin is covered. Kasah, cover, a near relative of kaphar, the atonement verb.
He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken. Quoted at John 19:36, itself echoing the Passover lamb's own unbroken bones.
The meek shall inherit the earth. Anav ranges from humble in spirit to poor and afflicted in circumstance.
Every man walketh in a vain shew. Betselem, in an image, the identical word as image of God at Genesis 1:27.

lemma: אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי oznayim karita li (Hebrew) / σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι soma de katertiso moi (LXX, behind Hebrews 10:5)
gist: Mine ears hast thou opened. Hebrews 10:5 quotes it as a body hast thou prepared me, following the Greek, not the Hebrew.

lemma: עָקֵב akev (heel; cf. Ya'akov, Jacob) · H6119
gist: Mine own familiar friend hath lifted up his heel against me. Akev, heel, the same root as Jacob's name, applied by Jesus to Judas's betrayal.
As the hart panteth after the water brooks. Arag, a rare verb for an audible cry of longing, not quiet heavy breathing.

lemma: כִּסְאֲךָ אֱלֹהִים kis'akha elohim · H3678 + H430
gist: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever. The king addressed directly as elohim, quoted of the Son at Hebrews 1:8.
Be still, and know that I am God. Harpu is a military command: cease fire, stand down, not sit quietly.

lemma: מַשְׂכִּיל maskil (שָׂכַל sakal, be wise) · H4905
gist: Sing praises with understanding. Maskil, a term of uncertain meaning, also a mysterious label heading thirteen other psalms.

lemma: יַרְכְּתֵי צָפוֹן yarkete tsaphon (cf. Mount Zaphon) · H3411 + H6828
gist: Mount Zion, on the sides of the north. Yarkete tsaphon, likely naming Mount Zaphon, the Canaanite storm-god Baal's own mythological mountain.

lemma: חוֹלַלְתִּי chollalti (חוּל chul/chil, writhe in birth) · H2342
gist: Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me. A statement about the depth of David's guilt, later read as a doctrine of universal inherited sin.
Create in me a clean heart. The verb is the one only God is ever allowed to do.
Renew a right spirit within me. The same noun runs through the next two verses meaning different things.

lemma: אַשְׁלִיךְ נַעֲלִי ashlich na'ali (cast my shoe) · H7993 / H5275
gist: Over Edom will I cast out my shoe. A legal gesture claiming ownership, the same custom used to finalize a transaction at Ruth 4:7.

lemma: רֹכֵב בָּעֲרָבוֹת rokev ba'aravot (cf. Ugaritic rkb 'rpt) · H7392 + H6160
gist: Extol him that rideth upon the heavens. The title matches rider of the clouds, Baal's own standing epithet in Ugaritic.

lemma: לָקַחְתָּ מַתָּנוֹת lakachta matanot (received gifts) · H3947 + H4979
gist: Thou hast received gifts for men. Ephesians 4:8 quotes it as gave gifts to men, matching the Aramaic Targum's own reading, not the Hebrew or Greek Old Testament.

lemma: יִנּוֹן Yinnon (נוּן nun/נִין nin, sprout/continue) · H5125
gist: His name shall be continued as long as the sun. Yinnon, a word used only here, read by Jewish tradition as one of the Messiah's own names.

lemma: כָּלוּ תְפִלּוֹת דָּוִד בֶּן־יִשָׁי kalu tefillot David ben-Yishai · H8615
gist: The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended. Yet David's name appears on psalms well after this point.

lemma: לִוְיָתָן Leviathan (רָאשֵׁי livyatan rashei, heads of) · H3882
gist: Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces. The multi-headed sea-dragon of the same chaos-combat imagery already met in Genesis.
God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods. One Hebrew word, both times.
I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God. Histopheph, a verb used only here, meaning to sit at the threshold.
Free among the dead, like the slain that lie in the grave. Chophshi ordinarily means released or liberated, an odd, bitter word choice for death.

lemma: רַהַב Rahab (chaos-monster, heh) / רָחָב Rachav (Rahab of Jericho, chet) · H7294 / H7343
gist: Thou hast broken Rahab in pieces. A different word entirely from Rahab the woman of Jericho.

lemma: עוֹלָם olam (מֵעוֹלָם עַד־עוֹלָם me'olam ad olam) · H5769
gist: From everlasting to everlasting, thou art God. Olam names indefinite, out-of-sight time rather than philosophical eternity.
The destruction that wasteth at noonday. Some ancient versions personify qeteb as a demon; the Hebrew itself, and the King James, keep it impersonal.

lemma: יְהוָה מָלָךְ YHWH malakh · H3068 + H4427
gist: The LORD reigneth. Malakh could mean has become king, marking a specific moment, or reigns, describing an ongoing state.

lemma: מְרִיבָה Meribah (רִיב riv, strive) / מַסָּה Massah (נָסָה nasah, test) · H4809 / H4532
gist: As at Meribah, and as in the day of Massah. Both place names and, simultaneously, the ordinary words for strife and testing.

lemma: וְלֹא אֲנַחְנוּ / וְלוֹ אֲנַחְנוּ velo anachnu (ketiv, not) / velo anachnu (qere, to him) · H3808 / לוֹ (le + 3ms suffix, no independent Strong's number)
gist: It is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves. Or: and his we are. One preserved letter apart, and Jewish scribal tradition marks both readings.

lemma: מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב mizrach u-ma'arav · H4217 + H4628
gist: As far as the east is from the west. A deliberately chosen pair of directions with no meeting point, unlike north and south.
Who maketh his angels spirits. Ruach, the same word for wind, breath, and spirit, used twice in one sentence about natural forces.

lemma: בַּרְזֶל בָּאָה נַפְשׁוֹ barzel ba'ah naphsho (his soul came into iron) · H1270 + H935 + H5315
gist: The iron entered into his soul. The Hebrew more literally reads his soul came into iron, a difficult phrase ancient translators handled differently.

lemma: יְהוָה YHWH · H3068 / אֲדֹנִי adoni · H113
gist: The LORD said unto my Lord. Two different Hebrew words, and English uses one.
Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints. Or: grievous, costly, in the LORD's sight.

lemma: רֹאשׁ פִּנָּה rosh pinnah · H7218 + H6438
gist: The head stone of the corner. Either the foundation stone set first, or the capstone set last at the very top.

lemma: הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא hoshia na (Hosanna) · H3467 + H4994
gist: Save now, I beseech thee, O LORD. Hoshia na, the Hebrew behind Hosanna, is a plea for rescue, not originally a shout of praise.

lemma: מֵאַיִן יָבֹא עֶזְרִי me'ayin yavo ezri (from where does my help come) · H370
gist: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. Or: unto the hills, where does my help come from?

lemma: כֵּן יִתֵּן לִידִידוֹ שֵׁנָא ken yiten lididho shena · H8142
gist: So he giveth his beloved sleep. Or: he gives to his beloved even in their sleep, provision without anxious toil.
Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect. Golmi, an unformed, still-shapeless mass, the word later Judaism borrowed to name the golem.

lemma: רֹאשִׁי rosh'i (my head), verse marked as textually uncertain in the critical apparatus
gist: Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness... for yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities. A notoriously difficult Hebrew text; ancient and modern versions diverge sharply.

lemma: נ (nun), the fourteenth Hebrew letter, its acrostic line absent from the Masoretic Text
gist: The LORD is faithful in all his words, and holy in all his works. Missing between this and the previous verse: an entire nun line, preserved outside the Masoretic Text.

lemma: עוּגָב ugav (reed pipe, simple wind instrument) · H5748
gist: Praise him with stringed instruments and organs. Ugav, an ancient reed or wind instrument, not the keyboard instrument organ now names.
Human, and the ground he was taken from. The pun is the point.
Lord, master, sir. An ordinary word, and also what is said aloud in place of the divine name.
Age. The noun behind the adjective English renders eternal.
Resurrection. The noun means a standing up again, and it is a bodily word.
Apostle. The noun simply means one who is sent, with authority to act for the sender.
Iniquity. The act, the guilt, and the consequence, in one noun.
Flesh, body, meat, and by extension kinship and human frailty.
Kingdom. Closer to kingship or reign than to a territory.
Covenant. A binding arrangement, and in Hebrew you cut one rather than make one.
Joy. Built on the same root as grace, which is not an accident.
Sin, and also the offering that deals with it. One word for both.
Life. Plural in form, singular in meaning.
Wisdom. It includes skill with your hands.
Time as duration. The other half of the pair, and the one English defaults to.
Word, thing, matter, event. Speech and the thing spoken are one noun.
Servant. The word behind deacon, and it is not a lesser word than the one for slave.
To justify. A courtroom verb meaning to declare in the right, not to make good.
Righteousness. English splits this into righteousness and justice; Greek and Hebrew do not.
Slave. English versions mostly print servant, and the two are not the same relationship.
Glory. In ordinary Greek it meant opinion or reputation; the Septuagint loaded it with Hebrew weight.
Peace. In Greek it is mainly the absence of war; in the Bible it carries Hebrew shalom.
Church. A civic word for a called-out assembly, with no religious content of its own.
God. The shortest word for deity, and also the name of the high god of Canaan.
Mercy. In the Septuagint it is the word chosen for Hebrew chesed, which is much larger.
God, gods, divine beings. A category word, and plural in form even when it means one.
Hope. Confident expectation, not wishing.
Land, earth, country. Which one it means is usually the whole question.
Gospel. In ordinary Greek it was the announcement of a royal victory or an emperor's accession.
Kinsman-redeemer. A legal role English has no word for at all.
Holy. The idea is set apart for a purpose, not morally spotless.
Sin. The word carries an image of a shot that misses.
Vapour, breath. The word Ecclesiastes repeats and English calls vanity.
Way. A road, and the first name the movement had for itself.
Endurance. The word is built on staying under a weight, not on waiting quietly.
Time. The right moment, as against time on a clock.
To call. The verb behind church, calling, and the word for those called out.
Glory. From a root meaning heavy. Weight before brightness.
To atone. The root sense is disputed between covering and wiping clean.
Priest. A functionary of the sanctuary, and the word used of foreign priests too.
Fellowship. A word for shared ownership and partnership, including in money.
World. The root idea is order and arrangement, which is why it also gives cosmetics.
Lord. Also sir, and also the Septuagint's replacement for the divine name.
Longsuffering. Literally long-tempered, the opposite of short-tempered.
Messenger. The same word is used of human envoys and of heavenly ones.
Witness. The English word martyr is the same Greek word, after what happened to the witnesses.
Anointed one. In the Old Testament it usually means the reigning king.
Death. Also personified, and paired with Sheol in the poetry.
King. The ordinary word, and the one behind Moloch and Melchizedek.
Repentance. The Greek noun is about a change of mind, and the Latin behind the English is about penance.
Justice, judgment, the right ordering of things, and also a legal decision.
Prophet. One who speaks for someone else, which is a job rather than a gift of prediction.
Soul, life, self, appetite, throat. The animals have one too.
Mind. Understanding and the faculty that does it, in one noun.
A long duration, an age, the far horizon. Usually flattened to forever.
Light. The first thing spoken into existence, and a standing image for life and favour.
Face, presence. Plural in form, and used of God constantly.
Transgression. A relational breach, closer to rebellion than to a slip.
To believe. In Greek that is closer to entrusting yourself than to agreeing with a claim.
Spirit. The same noun means wind and breath, exactly like Hebrew ruach.
Thy law. The Hebrew word is instruction, and the psalm has eight words for it.

lemma: (parallel texts: Psalm 18 / 2 Samuel 22, no single lemma)
gist: Psalm 18 and 2 Samuel 22 are two versions of the same song, close but not identical.

lemma: קוֹל יְהוָה qol YHWH (voice of the LORD, sevenfold) · H6963
gist: The voice of the LORD, seven times. A storm-theophany pattern closely paralleling Ugaritic hymns to the storm-god Baal.

lemma: אֱלֹהִים elohim / יְהוָה YHWH (systematic substitution) · H430 / H3068
gist: Psalm 53 duplicates Psalm 14 almost word for word, but replaces every LORD with God.

lemma: (acrostic structure, no single lemma) · cf. Psalm 119
gist: Psalms 9 and 10 together form a single acrostic, moving through the Hebrew alphabet letter by letter, a structure no translation can preserve.
Soul. The same word is rendered life a few verses away, and it translates Hebrew nephesh.
Holy. Set apart for a purpose, before it is anything about moral purity.
Flesh. Sometimes meat, sometimes the body, sometimes a whole orientation of life.
Peace. Wholeness and completeness, not merely the absence of conflict.
Name, and with it reputation, character and authority.
The realm of the dead. Not hell, and not nothing.
Body. The word Paul chooses for the church, and deliberately not the other one.
To save. One Greek verb covers rescue from danger, healing from disease, and eternal salvation.

lemma: ἀγάπη agape · G26 / φιλία philia · G5373 / στοργή storge (compounds only) / ἔρως eros (absent)
gist: Four Greek words for love, and two of them never appear in the New Testament.
Instruction, teaching. Law is a narrow rendering of a wide word.
Army, host. The plural in the title LORD of Hosts.
Righteousness, and just as often justice. English splits them.

ref: When the English moved, not the Greek
lemma: Not a lemma: an English dictionary problem
gist: Roughly a hundred and thirty-six King James phrases now say something the Greek and Hebrew never said. Not one of them is a translation error.
Hand, and with it power, agency and control.
To fear, and also to revere. The same problem English has with awe.
To save, deliver, rescue. The root behind the names Joshua and Jesus.
Seed. Singular in form, collective in sense, and Paul builds an argument on that.
Life. Greek has a second word for life as a span, and the Gospel of John never uses it.
I AM, or I WILL BE. The Hebrew is one form and it carries both.
Hear, O Israel. In Hebrew, hearing that does not change anything is not hearing.
Love God with all your heart. The Hebrew word is about the thinking, deciding self, not the feelings English now hears.
Hebrew has one word for love, and this is the chapter that proves how wide it is.
Virgin or young woman. One Hebrew word, seven occurrences, and an argument that has run for two thousand years.
Breath, wind, and Spirit. One Hebrew word, three English words, all in one vision.
Daily bread. The word translated daily occurs twice in all of Greek literature, here and in Luke's version of the prayer.

lemma: καρδία kardia · G2588 / διάνοια dianoia · G1271
gist: Deuteronomy lists three. Jesus lists four. The extra one tells you how the first century read the original.
No room at the inn. The word is not the word for inn. Luke uses it again for the upper room at 22:11, and he has a different word for a commercial inn at 10:34.
Storge never stands alone in the New Testament. It turns up inside compounds, and the one that names it as missing is the one most readers meet.
Faith in Christ, or the faithfulness of Christ. Greek does not say which.
Christ is the end of the law. Stopped, or arrived at? The Greek noun means both.
Two Greek words for love welded into one, and English has to pick a phrase.
Be filled with the Spirit. The Greek is a command to keep being filled, continuously, and by someone else.
Husbands, love your wives. The word is agape, and the word you would expect is the one that is missing.
